key_insight: STReasoner empowers large language models to perform explicit spatio-temporal reasoning on time series by combining a dedicated benchmark (ST-Bench) with spatial-aware reinforcement learning, enabling synthesis of temporal dynamics, spatial dependencies, and textual context for interpretable decisions.
problem_solved: Existing time-series work emphasizes predictive accuracy but fails to support explicit spatio-temporal and etiological reasoning (e.g., identifying causes and spatial propagation), and lacks benchmarks and training strategies to teach LLMs to reason across space, time, and text.
method: Introduce ST-Bench: a benchmark of four core tasks (including etiological reasoning) designed to evaluate explicit spatio-temporal reasoning capabilities.
Fine-tune LLMs with Spatial-Aware Reinforcement Learning that conditions policy updates on spatial encodings and rewards spatially-consistent, explanation-aligned actions.

Fuse modalities by conditioning the model on time-aware inputs and structured spatial representations (e.g., graph/grid encodings) so it can jointly synthesize temporal dynamics, spatial dependencies, and textual context.
impact: Provides practitioners a path to turn LLMs from black-box predictors into agents that reason about how events propagate in space and time—useful for high-stakes domains like traffic management, power grids, and epidemic response where interpretable, cause-aware decisions matter.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: LLM + spatial encoder + RL training loop (policy, reward, spatial-aware loss).
ST-Bench overview: a 4-task matrix with example inputs/outputs (including an etiological reasoning example).
Spatio-temporal map sequence: animated snapshots showing propagation and the model's reasoning annotations.
Performance chart: reasoning-focused metrics (explainability/causal correctness) comparing STReasoner vs predictive baselines.
paper_title: STReasoner: Empowering LLMs for Spatio-Temporal Reasoning in Time Series via Spatial-Aware Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Juntong Ni, Shiyu Wang, Ming Jin, Qi He, Wei Jin
